title: Fall of France: Breakthrough at Sedan (12-20 May 1940)

briefing.historical: By 12 May 1940 the German Army Group A had driven armoured divisions through the Ardennes and stood on the Meuse. Guderian's XIX Panzer Corps entered Sedan that day (S08); Hoth's XV Corps and Reinhardt's XLI Corps closed on the river further north. The French Second and Ninth Armies held the Meuse line while the First Army and the BEF moved forward under Plan D toward the Dyle (S13).
briefing.situation: The Meuse crossings decide the campaign. As the Germans, force the river, widen the bridgehead and race for the Channel at Abbeville before the French armoured reserves can react. As the Allies, hold the Meuse, counter-attack with the DCRs and keep the corridor to the sea closed. The scenario ends 20 May 1940, the day the Germans reached the coast (S06).

playableNations.summary: Armoured breakthrough with a strong spearhead and a long supply line.

AIRFIELD POSITION POLICY (internal): airfield coordinates are nearest-village/airfield gazetteer values recalled to 0.01 deg; accuracy +/-0.15 deg. Where a Geschwader Stab base lies outside the map bbox, a Gruppe base inside the map is used (KG 2, KG 4, KG 53); KG 51 and KG 55 (all bases outside the bbox) and Lysander squadrons are omitted.

GAME-SCALE ABSTRACTION (internal, not a historical source): manpower, equipment points, morale/experience/organisation values, nation resources and income are nominal game values chosen for balance by type/nation. They are NOT historical strengths.
Modern gazetteer coordinates (Wikipedia/GeoNames, rounded to 0.01 deg) for towns, cities, ports and fortresses. Maginot fortress coordinates are approximate (+/- 0.05 deg).

POSITION POLICY (internal): no source gives division-level start positions. Unit positions are approximate sector/assembly-area anchors inferred from the operational axes in S06-S08 and S13, with a small deterministic spread inside the sector. Every unit position is APPROXIMATE.

BORDER POLICY (internal): initialControl polygons are coarse hand-drawn approximations of 1939/1940 borders (Alsace-Lorraine French, Saar German, Luxembourg unclaimed) and ignore coastline detail; caveat: not survey-accurate.
